summary: Strong change overall: I re-ran the author's mutation checks and added three of my own, and the per-engine duplication is empirically justified — deleting the 402 branch from openai_transcreation alone fails exactly 3 tests, all in test_openai_transcreation.py, because each engine carries its own copy of the branch. The integration level is also already covered: test_job_distributed_publish.py:562 drives news_bot.job() with a real DB and asserts no strike / attempt_count 0 / row still pending / nothing published, test_job_distributed_publish.py:767 pins _publish_with_retries -> 'held', and test_llm_outage_hold.py pins the _fallback_publish contract. The engine->job seam is sound because test_gemini_transcreation.py:327 pins that ClaudeOutageError is one class identity across all engines and llm_transcreation, so a new end-to-end 402->held test would be redundant and should NOT be added. Two real defects remain: one new test has zero mutation-killing power (the entire type guard can be deleted with 1639/1639 still passing), and the shared-rule claim is factually false for the gemini engine, which classifies 413/451 as an outage — the exact queue-head wedge the change's own comments forbid.

findings.issue: Litmus failure, verified by mutation: I deleted the entire guard from _llm_common._is_account_level_status (both the `isinstance(code, bool)` and the `not isinstance(code, int)` clauses, leaving `return getattr(exc, 'status_code', None) in _ACCOUNT_LEVEL_STATUS_CODES`) and ran the full suite — 1639 passed, 450 subtests passed. All three assertions (missing attribute, None, '402') return False through plain frozenset membership whether or not the guard exists, because no None/str/bool is equal to 402, 407 or 408. The bool clause is unreachable by construction on top of that: `True in frozenset({402,407,408})` is False, so the docstring claim in _llm_common.py:88 ('bool is excluded explicitly — True == 1 would otherwise let a truthy non-code slip through') describes an impossible scenario. The test therefore documents a contract it cannot enforce and gives false confidence that the guard is load-bearing.
findings.recommendation: Preferred: delete the guard and the test. Reduce the helper body to `return getattr(exc, 'status_code', None) in _ACCOUNT_LEVEL_STATUS_CODES` and drop the two docstring paragraphs about bool — behaviour is byte-identical and there is then nothing untested. If the guard is kept as intent-documentation, make it observable so the test can kill a mutant: the only reachable difference is a status_code whose __eq__ raises or returns a truthy non-bool. Add `class _Weird: __eq__ = lambda self, other: (_ for _ in ()).throw(RuntimeError('boom'))` and assert `self.assertFalse(_is_account_level_status(self._Err(_Weird())))` — that assertion fails (RuntimeError propagates out of the `in`) when the isinstance guard is removed, so it actually pins the guard. Keep the existing None/'402'/missing-attribute assertions only as documentation, and stop counting them as coverage.

findings.issue: The new test class is introduced as 'The one rule every engine shares for status codes the SDKs have no dedicated exception class for', but gemini_transcreation._classify_exception never imports or calls _is_account_level_status. Verified against the installed SDK: gemini maps 402 -> ClaudeOutageError (accidentally right), but also 413 -> ClaudeOutageError and 451 -> ClaudeOutageError, because its ClientError branch returns outage for every code except 400 and 422. That is precisely the failure the change's own comments say must never happen ('an outage pins the row to the queue head... a novel article-specific code would stop the channel'). Three engines are now pinned to the conservative default and the fourth silently violates it with zero test coverage — test_gemini_transcreation.py exercises only 429/401/400/500. Currently dormant (.env carries only OPENROUTER_API_KEY, so llm_transcreation auto-selects openrouter), but LLM_PROVIDER=gemini activates it, and the false 'every engine' claim will mislead whoever adds engine number five.
findings.recommendation: Two-line fix plus tests. In gemini_transcreation._classify_exception, route the ClientError branch through the shared helper so the invariant is genuinely shared: replace the `if code in (400, 422): return ClaudeTranscreationError(...)` / fallthrough-to-outage pair with `if _is_account_level_status(exc) or code in (401, 403, 404, 429): return ClaudeOutageError(...)` then `return ClaudeTranscreationError(...)` as the default (gemini's ClientError sets both .code and .status_code, so the helper reads it unchanged). Then add to tests/test_gemini_transcreation.py::TestExceptionClassification, matching that file's existing _make_client_error style: `def test_account_level_402_is_outage` asserting `assertIsInstance(gemini_transcreation._classify_exception(_make_client_error(402)), ClaudeOutageError)`, and `def test_article_level_413_451_stay_per_article` looping `for code in (413, 451)` with subTest asserting ClaudeTranscreationError. If instead the decision is to leave gemini alone, correct the TestAccountLevelStatus docstring to 'shared by the claude / openai / openrouter engines; gemini keeps its own ClientError mapping' so the claim stops being false.

findings.issue: Inconsistent with the file's own convention and strictly weaker than the sibling engines. Every other test in that TestExceptionClassification class drives transcreate_via_claude with a mock client; only these two call _classify_exception directly (test_classifier_passes_through_already_wrapped is legitimately classifier-level since it has no client path). Verified consequence: I inserted `except openai.APIStatusError as exc: raise ClaudeTranscreationError(...)` ahead of the `except openai.OpenAIError` clause at openai_transcreation.py:345 — both new tests stayed green; only the pre-existing rate-limit/auth/500 tests caught it. The new tests contribute nothing toward pinning that a 402 raised by the client actually escapes transcreate_via_claude as ClaudeOutageError, which is what the openrouter and claude versions do.
findings.recommendation: Match the sibling engines and the file's convention — the helpers already exist. Replace the body of each loop iteration with the client path: `client = _make_client_returning(_make_status_error(code))` then `with patch.object(openai_transcreation, '_load_prompt', return_value='X'): with self.assertRaises(ClaudeOutageError): openai_transcreation.transcreate_via_claude(SAMPLE_ARTICLE, client=client)` (and ClaudeTranscreationError for the 413/451 test). Keeps the subTest structure, adds no new helper, and makes the engine trio symmetric.

findings.issue: The fix only fires when the SDK raises. openrouter_transcreation.transcreate_via_claude catches openai.OpenAIError from chat.completions.create; if the credit error arrives instead as HTTP 200 with an error object in the body and no choices (a documented OpenRouter behaviour for some provider-side errors), execution reaches `response.choices[0].message.content`, the AttributeError/IndexError/TypeError handler raises ClaudeTranscreationError('OpenRouter response shape unexpected: ...'), and the article takes a per-article strike — the exact 3-strike loss the change exists to prevent. Neither test_openrouter_transcreation.py nor test_openai_transcreation.py has any test for the response-shape branch or the empty-content branch: grep for 'response shape unexpected' and 'content is empty' returns zero hits across the whole tests/ tree. I could not confirm the 2026-07-14 wire format — work/llm-402-outage/ contains only change.diff, and logs/ has no incident capture — which is why this is filed minor rather than major.
findings.recommendation: First confirm the wire format from the incident logs on the server; if the 402 arrived as an HTTP status the existing coverage is sufficient and this can be closed. If it arrived in the body, pin the behaviour with a test in TestExceptionClassification: build `resp = MagicMock(); resp.choices = []; resp.error = {'code': 402, 'message': 'Insufficient credits'}` (or `del resp.choices` for the AttributeError shape), feed it via `_make_client_returning(resp)`, and assert `with self.assertRaises(ClaudeOutageError)`. That test fails today, and the accompanying fix is a pre-parse check in transcreate_via_claude before reading choices: `err = getattr(response, 'error', None)` and, when `isinstance(err, dict) and err.get('code') in _ACCOUNT_LEVEL_STATUS_CODES`, `raise ClaudeOutageError(f'OpenRouter in-body error {err.get("code")}')`. Regardless of the outcome, add one test for the current response-shape branch asserting ClaudeTranscreationError, so that error path stops being wholly uncovered.

findings.issue: Answering the depth question precisely: duplication across engines is justified and I proved it — deleting the branch from openai_transcreation.py alone fails 3 tests, all inside test_openai_transcreation.py, since each engine holds its own copy of `if _is_account_level_status(exc)`. Repetition of the individual codes is not. 402, 407 and 408 are each asserted in all three engine files plus the helper test, i.e. four times per code, but they come from a single shared frozenset in _llm_common, so dropping 407 from that set is killed four times over while adding no distinct failure mode. Each engine test only needs to prove its own branch is wired to the helper, which one account code and one article code establish.
findings.recommendation: Optional trim, no coverage lost. Keep TestAccountLevelStatus in test_llm_common.py as the exhaustive owner of the code set (it already loops 402/407/408 and 400/413/414/415/451/499). In the three engine files reduce the parametrize/loop to two representative codes — `@pytest.mark.parametrize('status_code', [402])` for the outage case and `[413]` for the per-article case in test_claude_transcreation.py, and the same single-code pairs in the two unittest files. Verify after trimming that deleting any one engine's `if _is_account_level_status(exc):` line still fails that engine's tests; it will, since the branch is what those tests exercise. Low priority — cost of the extra codes is two parametrize entries.

findings.issue: Stale name and docstring in the test file that owns the slot-loop outage contract this change depends on. The name says 'routes via google' and the docstring asserts '_fallback_publish itself short-circuits to Google internally on the active-fallback flag', but that behaviour was deliberately removed by the 2026-06-11 hold-and-wait decision and tests/test_llm_outage_hold.py:139 explicitly pins the opposite ('A previously-set is_fallback_active() == True must NOT short-circuit to Google', with mock_google wired to raise AssertionError if called). The assertions themselves are still correct (publish fires once, via_review=False), so nothing fails — the test just documents behaviour the codebase forbids, directly in the area this change touches.
findings.recommendation: Rename to test_fallback_active_still_routes_through_fallback_publish and rewrite the docstring to the current contract: 'is_fallback_active() == True must not skip the slot — the loop still calls _fallback_publish so the LLM is retried and a recovery can be detected; there is no Google short-circuit (see tests/test_llm_outage_hold.py::test_fallback_active_does_not_route_to_google).' Assertions stay as they are.
